messages:
Sophie (support): FYI — FinOps customer reports objects are still showing up in search after TTL expired under the default 30d retention. They attempted deletes and hit a 403 KMS error. Can we triage?
Liam (eng-sre): Can you paste the object IDs, the exact API call, and the 403 response body? Also confirm if this is hosted vs dedicated and whether keys were rotated recently.
Sophie (support): Hosted API. ObjIDs: obj_8f3b2e, obj_a12df9. Delete call: `DELETE /v1/objects/obj_8f3b2e` returns 403 with body `{\"error\":\"kms:Decrypt failed\",\"code\":\"KMS_ACCESS_DENIED\"}`.
Sophie (support): Customer also attached audit log entries showing tombstone events at 2025-10-12T14:03:21Z, but search still returns hits for those IDs.
AuditBot: AUDIT LOG: {timestamp: 2025-10-12T14:03:21Z, actor: system.deleter, action: tombstone_create, id: obj_8f3b2e, retention_policy: default_30d} 
Mike (support-eng): Quick check — can you run a storage meta query? `GET /internal/storage/objects/obj_8f3b2e/meta` — does it show deleted=true and tombstone_ts set?
Sophie (support): Storage meta shows `deleted: true` and tombstone_ts present. Search query `GET /v1/search?q=obj_8f3b2e` still returns a hit with `index_state: live`.
Liam (eng-sre): That points at an indexer backlog or failed reindex. Any indexer errors around 14:03 in logs?
Andrew (eng-infra): We ran a KMS key rotation in that region on 2025-10-12 at ~13:50 UTC. There were transient 403s for some workers while propagation completed (approx ~7m window).
Rachel (security): If indexer/reindex workers couldn't decrypt tombstone payloads during rotation they may have skipped tombstone processing. Need to check whether tombstones were queued or dropped.
Anya (legal): The customer had a compliance hold flag earlier and cleared it at 2025-10-12T15:00Z. Legal needs a clear timeline: when retention started, when hold was toggled, and when the system actually removed or reindexed.
Mike (support-eng): I ran a short repro locally: 1) create object, 2) set TTL 0, 3) wait for deleter to tombstone, 4) indexer attempted reindex but logged `decrypt failed: access denied` during simulated rotation. Repro snippet:
````
# reproduce: delete then watch indexer
curl -X DELETE "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj_repro" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
# expected: 202 + tombstone event; observed: tombstone created in storage but indexer logged decrypt error and left index entry
````
Liam (eng-sre): Action items: (1) eng-infra to run a targeted reindex/resync for the time window covering the rotation (13:45-14:15 UTC), (2) security to verify no tombstone payloads were irretrievably dropped, (3) support to provide the customer an initial timeline and mitigation (forced reindex + integrity report).
Andrew (eng-infra): Kicking off targeted resync job now: job id `resync-20251012-01`. ETA about 30m. I'll attach logs when done.
Sophie (support): I'll update the customer: targeted reindex is running; we'll provide an audit bundle with tombstone + hold toggle timestamps and an integrity confirmation once resync finishes. Also asking if they want expedited purge while this runs. :thumbsup: 
Anya (legal): Include explicit hold toggle timestamps and a signed confirmation of removal from search index when complete. Legal will need that for the compliance record.
Sophie (support): Copy — filing follow-ups. Will circle back when resync completes or if we find dropped tombstones.
